status.label: Reproduce Word markup leakage
status.detail: The report gives exact Word-to-Markdown steps and unwanted conditional markup; a broader formatting feature is not a confirmed fix.

next_action.label: Capture Word clipboard fixture and normalize markup
next_action.reason: The remaining discriminator is the HTML clipboard structure and conversion behavior, which a maintainer can inspect.

judgment.rationale: The Word Title-style reproduction and literal conditional-markup output are actionable. Current MarkdownConverter strips styles and a limited list of elements but has no explicit Word conditional-markup normalization. The separate formatting roadmap does not prove this bug has been fixed.
evidence: On 0.81.1, copying Word Title-style TEXT and choosing Paste as Markdown emits <![if !supportLineBreakNewLine]> and <![endif]> instead of the requested heading.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/33261#issuecomment-2197525850 explicitly keeps this report open as a bug.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/33109 discusses broader formatting/custom-action ideas and references this report as a possible beneficiary, not a delivered fix.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/src/modules/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPaste.Core/MarkdownConverter.cs removes inline styles and script/sup/o:p elements before ReverseMarkdown conversion.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the provided Word example, preserve its clipboard HTML as a test fixture and normalize unsupported Word markup without losing content.

fix_assessment.rationale: The observed cleanup gap supports a focused conversion fix. The broader custom-formatting work and headless-converter refactor do not establish coverage of this exact Word fixture.

proposed_fixes.title: Normalize Word clipboard HTML before Markdown conversion
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: Word-specific conditional declarations survive cleanup and are serialized into Markdown, while stripping inline styling before interpreting semantic paragraph styles can lose title/heading intent. The exact Word HTML fixture is needed to confirm both branches.
plan: Reproduce the public Word Title-style TEXT example and capture its CF_HTML fragment locally as a sanitized fixture; compare Title and Heading 1 so their semantics are not assumed equivalent.

In src/modules/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPaste.Core/MarkdownConverter.cs, add targeted handling for Word conditional artifacts before conversion, retaining visible fallback text rather than removing whole conditional regions blindly.

Preserve recognized semantic heading information before removing styles, but map Word Title to a heading only after defining that supported behavior; accept equivalent valid Markdown syntax rather than requiring Setext formatting exclusively.
Add fixture tests for Word conditional line-break markers, Title/heading paragraphs, ordinary text, lists, tables and intentional text that resembles markup.
verification: The exact Word TEXT reproduction no longer emits <![if ...]> or <![endif]> tokens.
Heading semantics match the agreed mapping, using valid ATX or Setext output without losing TEXT.
Ordinary HTML/Word lists, tables and line breaks retain content and existing supported formatting.

confidence.rationale: The literal output and upstream cleanup code align, but actual CF_HTML and Title-versus-heading semantics must be checked before implementation.

issue_context.summary: Pasting a Word Title-style paragraph as Markdown leaks Word conditional line-break markup and does not produce the heading representation the reporter expected.
known_information: The report supplies a three-step reproduction and exact expected/actual text.
The maintainer left the bug open and linked broader formatting work.
The live issue is open, unassigned and labeled Priority-3/Advanced Paste.
inferences: Word-specific markup cleanup is a likely conversion boundary.
The Title style may be represented differently from a semantic HTML heading; its Markdown mapping is not established by the report alone.
issue_context.analysis: The report already gives a local reproduction. Maintainers should capture their own clipboard fixture rather than asking the reporter for another generic ZIP or treating a roadmap link as existing-fix coverage.
initial_investigation: Read the report, its sole comment and the related #33109 discussion.
Verified current upstream MarkdownHelper extracts the HTML fragment and delegates to AdvancedPaste.Core.MarkdownConverter.
Read MarkdownConverter.CleanNodes: it removes style attributes and selected elements, with no explicit supportLineBreakNewLine handling.
The converter's recent #50834 headless refactor moves the conversion into Core but does not itself establish a Word-markup fix.

reproduce.title: Word Title conditional-markup leakage
reproduce.version_requirement: Compare reported 0.81.1 with a current supported build; record Word version.
prerequisites: A plain-text destination such as VS Code
reproduce.setup_prompt: Create a new local test Word document containing the single word TEXT with the built-in Title style. Add separate control paragraphs using Heading 1 and Normal. Use no user documents or confidential content. Prepare a text editor destination and capture only these test paragraphs' clipboard HTML for regression fixtures.
steps: 1. Copy the Word paragraph containing TEXT with Title style.
2. Use Advanced Paste's built-in Paste as Markdown action into the text editor.
3. Compare output with the issue's literal conditional markers and capture the sanitized clipboard HTML fragment.
4. Repeat for Heading 1 and Normal to separate markup cleanup from the desired Title-style mapping.
reproduce.expected_result: No Word conditional declarations leak into Markdown; content remains intact and heading output follows the supported semantics.

actions.label: Review Word HTML normalization plan
actions.note: Validate the CF_HTML fixture and Title semantics before changing cleanup.
